set: English Drill 3: Comprehension: five real GPSC passages

sections.name: English drill: Comprehension: five real GPSC passages

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Most malnutrition is invisible. Consistent undernutrition, together with bouts of infection and diarrhoea, can retard growth so gradually as to go unnoticed by the mother. Unless a child is seriously underweight or shows obvious signs of malnutrition (listlessness, discoloured hair, irritability, frequent crying, distended stomach) his condition of undernutrition may not be visible to the mother. For timely prevention of malnutrition, the UNICEF has been using the simple inexpensive method of growth monitoring charts which help mothers see whether or not their children are growing and gaining weight correctly, and thus can be an effective aid to sound child health and nutrition. The first requirement for children and adults who are undernourished and living at subsistence level is adequate quantity of food. The next is nutritious food, containing all the elements necessary to support life and maintain good health.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: The World Health Organization is popularly known as W.H.O. in brief. It is a specialized agency of the United Nations and was established in 1948. International health workers can be seen working in all kinds of surroundings: in deserts, jungles, mountains, coconut groves, and rice fields. They help the sick to attain health and the healthy to maintain their health. This global health team helps the local health workers in stopping the spread of what are called the communicable diseases, like cholera. These diseases can be spread from one country to another and so can be a threat to world health. W.H.O. assists different national health authorities not only in controlling diseases but also in preventing them. Total prevention is possible in a number of ways, such as vaccination and spraying of houses with substances which kill disease-carrying insects.

p3.title: Passage 3
paras: When talking about overeating, obesity and other conditions arising from affluence and plenty, we may tend to overlook the fact that ours is a country where a large percentage of the population subsists on too little food and hardly gets a square meal a day. Even if meals are available, they lack the essential nutrients such as protein, fats, vitamins and minerals. Millions of Indian children are living in poverty. An estimated three million die every year owing to certain preventable conditions, including malnutrition. Carelessness of parents, unhygienic environment and poor health conditions and malnutrition make children more susceptible to disease. It will shock you to know that a major cause of blindness in India is the lack of vitamin A, which is found in abundance in carrots, leaves of drumstick trees, milk and green leafy vegetables.

p4.title: Passage 4
paras: Tradition means those ways of thinking and feeling which have come down to us from the past. We still have tremendous faith in the power of goodness. This again has nothing to do with religion. A national leader appealed to a group of dacoits of Madhya Pradesh to give up their criminal lives and start afresh. One by one, they came and laid down their arms. They did not surrender to force but to goodness. This took place in the year 1972, but it could easily be a legend of ancient times. Many people say such a thing could not have happened anywhere else in the world today. Happenings of this kind tell us that ours is a living and growing tradition. It is still taking in new influences and merging them with the old. If this stops, Indian tradition itself will die.

p5.title: Passage 5
paras: Stereotyping is a type of generalization which attributes traits or characteristics to everyone in a large group. People who stereotype tend to have fixed and unbending opinions. They respond to challenges by distorting reality, rather than reconsider their assumptions and conclusions, which they have labelled as the truth. What happens is that the facts are compared to the stereotype and then rejected, because they do not fit the stereotype. Stereotyping is often caused by ethno-centrism. The ramifications of stereotyping are that it forces us to choose sides, causes destructive competition, alienates us from others and leads to narrow thinking. We end up denying dignity to others, whom we stereotype, and generate unhappiness all around us.

questions.q: The passage implies that, when early signs of malnutrition go unnoticed, the immediate fallout is that this
opts: leads to undernutrition in the long run
questions.why: Inference: undernutrition 'may not be visible to the mother'. GPSC's two versions of this item gave different keys; B follows the text. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Junior Scale Officer), Apr 2024.

questions.q: Listlessness, discoloured hair, irritability, frequent crying and a distended stomach in a child indicate
questions.why: Detail: these are the 'obvious signs of malnutrition'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Junior Scale Officer), Apr 2024.

questions.q: Which word from the passage means "to delay or slow down the development of something"?
questions.why: Vocabulary from the passage. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Junior Scale Officer), Apr 2024.

questions.q: The term "subsistence" in the passage means
opts: the minimal resources needed to survive
a kind of matter with uniform properties
questions.why: Vocabulary in context: 'living at subsistence level'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Junior Scale Officer), Apr 2024.

questions.q: What simple method has UNICEF used for timely prevention of malnutrition?
questions.why: Detail: the fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Junior Scale Officer), Apr 2024.

questions.q: Which word in the passage means "contagious or infectious"?
questions.why: Vocabulary from the passage. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Block Development Officer), Nov 2023.

questions.q: "It is a specialized agency of the United Nations." Here "specialized" means
opts: made suitable for a particular purpose
questions.why: Vocabulary in context: an agency with a specific function. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Block Development Officer), Nov 2023.

questions.q: "W.H.O. assists national health authorities not only in controlling diseases but also in preventing them." This implies that W.H.O.
opts: helps more in control than prevention
helps both in controlling and in preventing diseases
questions.why: 'Not only … but also' = both. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Block Development Officer), Nov 2023.

questions.q: In "They help the sick to attain health", "they" refers to
questions.why: Reference question: points back to the previous sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Block Development Officer), Nov 2023.

questions.q: Why are communicable diseases a threat to world health, according to the passage?
opts: They can spread from one country to another
questions.why: Detail: the sixth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Block Development Officer), Nov 2023.

questions.q: The last sentence indirectly reveals that a large part of the population lacks
opts: knowledge that carrots contain vitamin A
the means to afford even an ordinary diet containing vitamin A
questions.why: Inference: vitamin A is in cheap common foods, yet people go blind for lack of it. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Assistant in Toxicology), Apr 2023.

questions.q: Even when meals are available, many people
questions.why: Detail: meals 'lack the essential nutrients'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Assistant in Toxicology), Apr 2023.

questions.q: Besides parental carelessness and unhygienic surroundings, which other causes of disease in children are named?
questions.why: Detail: the fifth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Assistant in Toxicology), Apr 2023.

questions.q: Which phrase in the passage is the opposite of poverty and scarcity?
questions.why: Antonym from the passage. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Assistant in Toxicology), Apr 2023.

questions.q: The word "susceptible" as used in the passage means
questions.why: Vocabulary in context: 'more susceptible to disease'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Assistant in Toxicology), Apr 2023.

questions.q: The tradition discussed in the passage is
questions.why: Detail: the passage ends with 'Indian tradition'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Junior Scale Officer), Feb 2024.

questions.q: Through the example of the dacoits, the passage indirectly implies that
opts: our tradition has tremendous faith in the power of goodness
they surrendered to a leader's appeal only
questions.why: Purpose of the example: it illustrates the second sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Junior Scale Officer), Feb 2024.

questions.q: "It could easily be a legend of ancient times" refers to
opts: the dacoits' surrender to goodness rather than force
questions.why: Reference: the event just described. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Junior Scale Officer), Feb 2024.

questions.q: According to the passage, Indian tradition lives and grows because
opts: it has nothing to do with religion
it absorbs new influences and merges them with the old
questions.why: Detail: the second-last sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Junior Scale Officer), Feb 2024.

questions.q: The word "legend" as used in the passage means
opts: a traditional story, popularly believed but unverified
questions.why: Vocabulary in context. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Junior Scale Officer), Feb 2024.

questions.q: People who stereotype are NOT likely to
opts: treat their opinions as the truth
questions.why: They distort reality 'rather than reconsider their assumptions'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Planning Officer), Apr 2023.

questions.why: Vocabulary. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Planning Officer), Apr 2023.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to "ramification"?
questions.why: Vocabulary: a ramification is a (usually unwelcome) consequence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Planning Officer), Apr 2023.
